text: Given list_type=Sender, entries=["attacker@contoso.com"], no_expiration=true, and no existing block entry for that sender, When exo_add_tenant_block_list_entry is called, Then the response reports result=added for that entry with its identity, value, list_type=Sender and expiration_date=null

Given a sender already present in the tenant block list, When exo_add_tenant_block_list_entry is called again for the same list_type and value, Then the response reports result=already_blocked for that entry and no New-TenantAllowBlockListItems call is issued for it

Given two entries in one call, one new and one already blocked, When exo_add_tenant_block_list_entry is called, Then the response reports the new one as added and the existing one as already_blocked in the same results list, and the write call carries only the new entry
Given entries=[], When exo_add_tenant_block_list_entry is called, Then the response is error.code=invalid_argument and no upstream call (neither Get- nor New-TenantAllowBlockListItems) is made

Given list_type="IP" (not one of the three supported values), When exo_add_tenant_block_list_entry is called, Then the response is error.code=invalid_argument whose message names Sender, Url and FileHash as the supported values

Given no_expiration=true and expiration_date="2026-12-01T00:00:00+00:00" both supplied, When exo_add_tenant_block_list_entry is called, Then the response is error.code=invalid_argument stating the two are mutually exclusive and no upstream call is made
Given expiration_date="2026-12-01T00:00:00" (no timezone offset), When exo_add_tenant_block_list_entry is called, Then the response is error.code=invalid_argument and no upstream call is made

Given neither no_expiration nor expiration_date is supplied, When exo_add_tenant_block_list_entry is called, Then neither NoExpiration nor ExpirationDate is present in the New-TenantAllowBlockListItems call parameters, and the response surfaces whatever ExpirationDate the mocked upstream assigns rather than a client-invented default

Given no Exchange Online credential headers on the request, When exo_add_tenant_block_list_entry is called, Then the response is error.code=not_configured (the same NO_CREDENTIALS envelope every other tool in this connector returns)

Given the mocked upstream answers New-TenantAllowBlockListItems with HTTP 403, When exo_add_tenant_block_list_entry is called, Then the response is error.code=unauthorized whose message explicitly names Security Administrator or Organization Management

Given a real tenant where the app-only credential has Exchange Administrator but not Security Administrator / Organization Management, When exo_add_tenant_block_list_entry is called against that tenant, Then Exchange's real 403 response body is captured and compared against this tool's unauthorized message for wording accuracy
precond: A real EXO tenant with an app registration that has Exchange.ManageAsApp consent and only the Exchange Administrator role assigned (not Security Administrator / Organization Management).
steps: Call exo_add_tenant_block_list_entry(list_type="Sender", entries=["test@example.com"], no_expiration=true) against the real tenant.
Record the raw HTTP status and response body Exchange returns.
Compare against the tool's error.code=unauthorized message produced from that real response.
expect: The tool's unauthorized message correctly reflects the real 403 Exchange returns for a Security-Administrator-only cmdlet called by an Exchange-Administrator-only credential; no misclassification as a different error code.
notes: Needs a real vendor account with a specific, narrower role grant than this connector's documented default (Exchange Administrator) -- not available in the design/dev flow. Per references/mcp-track.md §3, a missing test account does not block shipping; this case is tracked here for a real-tenant retest.

text: Given notes="requested by SOC" on a newly added entry, When exo_add_tenant_block_list_entry is called, Then Notes is forwarded to New-TenantAllowBlockListItems and the mocked upstream's echoed Notes value appears in that entry's result

The connector's three-way GDAP role consistency check (registered tools vs docs/gdap-role-map.yaml vs README's Tools table) passes with exo_add_tenant_block_list_entry present, mapped to Security Administrator / Organization Management in both the yaml and the README, distinct from the other 18 tools' Exchange Administrator

Given list_type="Url", entries=["http://evil.example/"], no_expiration=true, When exo_add_tenant_block_list_entry is called, Then the entry is added the same way a Sender entry is (result=added, list_type=Url echoed back)

Given list_type="FileHash", entries=["768a813668695ef2483b2bde7cf5d1b2db0423a0d3e63e498f3ab6f2eb13ea3"], no_expiration=true, When exo_add_tenant_block_list_entry is called, Then the entry is added the same way a Sender entry is (result=added, list_type=FileHash echoed back)

Given the tenant block list already has "Attacker@Contoso.com" (mixed case) and the caller requests entries=["attacker@contoso.com"] (lowercase), When exo_add_tenant_block_list_entry is called, Then the entry is reported already_blocked (case-insensitive match), not added again

Given two entries in one call where the mocked upstream's New-TenantAllowBlockListItems response reports a per-entry Error for one of them, When exo_add_tenant_block_list_entry is called, Then the failing entry is reported result=invalid with that message, and the other entry in the same call is still reported added
